entries.serverConfirmedReason: Price edits change what is invoiced and are role-checked per part on the server; the result (updated, forbidden, failed) is reported per part before the list is refreshed.
Receiving stock writes a ledger entry. On-hand quantity is derived, so the client must not show a new quantity before the server confirms it.
A stock adjustment writes a signed ledger entry. On-hand quantity is derived and must not be shown before the server confirms it.
Saving an item writes cost and retail prices together with the description. Prices stay server-confirmed.
Item creation assigns the server identity and has no deduplication contract. The list shows a pending row without article number, price or actions until the server answers.

Creating a transfer checks site membership and legal-entity boundaries and commits stock. The result is not predictable, and there is no deduplication contract. The list shows a pending row without a transfer number, quantity or status until the server answers.
Approval is version-checked and commits stock at the source. Availability and the resulting status are decided by the server.
Rejection is version-checked and releases the transfer. The server decides the resulting stock.
Cancellation is version-checked and releases reserved stock. The client cannot predict the resulting quantities.
Shipping is version-checked and books a stock movement. Quantities stay server-confirmed.
Receiving books stock into the destination under a version check. On-hand quantity is derived on the server.
Returning unreceived quantity writes a compensating stock movement under a version check.

Purchase-order creation assigns the order number and stores line prices. Numbering and prices stay server-confirmed, and there is no deduplication contract. The list shows a pending row without an order number, price or status until the server answers.
Marking a purchase order sent also moves linked parts reservations to ordered and recomputes requisitions. That stock effect is not predictable.
Goods receipt posts stock ledger entries and recomputes the order status. Quantities stay server-confirmed.
Adding lines writes quantities and unit costs and can change the order total. Prices and quantities stay server-confirmed.
Updating a line changes quantity or unit cost and the order total. The client must not show those figures before the server confirms them.
Deleting a line changes the order total and is guarded by the order status and linked reservations. The server decides.
Deletion is guarded by the purchase-order state. The server decides.
Vendor creation assigns the server identity and has no deduplication contract. The list shows a pending row without an account number until the server answers.
Deletion is refused while purchase orders, purchase invoices, vehicle purchases or vendor articles are linked. The server decides.
Customer creation assigns the server identity and runs duplicate and field validation; no deduplication contract exists, so the list shows a pending row until the server answers.
Deletion is guarded by the deletion policy (open orders, invoices, vehicles); the server decides and the client cannot predict or safely roll it back.
Consent events are an append-only legal record with server-assigned sequence and revision; the effective status is computed by the server.
Adding a party can change the main contact and the customer's vehicle list; the server validates the period and role.
Ending a party changes the main contact and period records; the server validates and computes the result.
Vehicle creation runs identity resolution (FIN/plate uniqueness) and assigns the server identity; no deduplication contract exists.
Identity resolution calls a catalogue lookup and rewrites derived vehicle data; the result is not predictable.
Purchase creation assigns the purchase number and cost basis and checks the fiscal lock date.
Purchase patches change price, tax treatment and cost basis, which the server recalculates and validates against the lock date.
Receiving books the vehicle into stock and writes the vehicle ledger; a financial and stock effect the client cannot predict.
Deletion is guarded by the deletion policy and the purchase state; the server decides.
Sale creation reserves the vehicle (contested resource), assigns the sale number and calculates price and tax.
Sale patches change price, discounts, tax treatment and warranty terms, which the server recalculates.
Finalizing a sale is a fiscal posting: document numbers, ledger entries, stock status and lock date are authoritative on the server.
A trade-in changes the sale price and tax totals and creates a vehicle purchase; calculated by the server.
Removing a trade-in recalculates the sale totals and removes the linked purchase; calculated by the server.
Replacing the equipment set revalidates the marketplace listing and is a whole-set write with server-side catalogue checks.
Import preview parses an uploaded document and stores an import record; a long-running operation with server-assigned results.
Applying an import is version-checked (fingerprint and version) and rewrites vehicle and Pickerl data; imports stay server-confirmed.
Recording a Pickerl inspection recomputes the due date and the due lists on the server.
Creating a marketplace listing is an external side effect with server-side validation of the channels.
Listing patches feed the external marketplace and its validation result; an external effect.
Channel patches publish or withdraw the listing on an external marketplace; an external effect.
The server assigns the draft identity and prices from the workshop order. There is no deduplication contract.
A discount changes the price and the tax. The server recalculates both.
Issuing posts the invoice. The number and the status are assigned by the server.
The PDF is the customer delivery of the invoice. The server builds the document.
Finalizing locks the invoice, assigns the official number and posts stock. The client waits for that result.
The server copies prices and assigns the draft identity from the sales order. There is no deduplication contract. The list shows a pending row without a number or a price.
Recording a payment changes the settled amount. The server is the authority for the payment.
Reconciliation matches the payment to the fiscal receipt. The server decides the match.
Cancelling a fiscal receipt is a fiscal cancellation. The server confirms it.
A purchase invoice carries vendor prices and tax. The server assigns the identity. There is no deduplication contract.
Editing a purchase invoice writes prices and tax. The server recalculates the totals.
Posting a purchase invoice is a posting. The status is server-authoritative.
Marking a purchase invoice paid is a payment. The server confirms it.
Deleting a purchase invoice is guarded by the server and removes a financial document.
Removing a line changes the price and the tax. The server recalculates the bill.
